newsitem.title: USA: US Congress ready to pass bank reform-Sen. D'Amato.
newsitem.headline: US Congress ready to pass bank reform-Sen. D'Amato.

text.p: Congress is poised to pass historic legislation modernising U.S. financial laws but strong backing from the Clinton administration is also required, Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato said Wednesday.

"The 105th Congress is well positioned to approve legislation to address the competitive imbalance among all financial service providers," the New York Republican said at a meeting of the New York State Bankers Association here. "But the real keys to our success will be the administration's legislative proposals as well as their commitment to its passage."
"The secretary of the Treasury must not only be part of the debate -- in my view, he must lead the charge," D'Amato added.

The influential senator has introduced a bill to break down the Depression-era laws separating banking from other financial service industries. Three similar measures are under consideration in the House of Representatives.
D'Amato said he was not wedded to any particular approach, calling his own bill "a starting point."

"Whether we realize it or not, a consensus has already formed on many of the issues that Congress, the regulators and various industries have been unable or unwilling to resolve over past decades," D'Amato said.
On other banking legislation, D'Amato predicted Congress would reject a Clinton proposal to impose examination fees on state-chartered banks.
"It was a bad idea in the past, and it's a bad idea now," D'Amato said.
D'Amato said he would push an initiative to prohibit surcharge fees at bank automated teller machines.
He also said the Federal Reserve System ought to pay interest on banks' demand deposits.
He told the banking group the $500 million the Fed is not paying now "properly belongs in your bottom line."
D'Amato said he would hold hearings on the demand deposit issue.
